chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār and Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from the one who informed him, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Ismāʿīl ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh was with him, so he said: “My son, recite the muṣḥaf.” He said: “I am not in a state of wudu (ablution).” He said: “Do not touch the writing of the Book, but touch the paper and recite it.”

key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the written text of the Qur'an
key_terms.الْمُصْحَفَ: the written codex of the Qur'an
key_terms.الْوَرَقَ: the paper or pages of the muṣḥaf
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Can a person without wudu (ablution) touch the muṣḥaf and recite the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates a ruling concerning reciting the muṣḥaf while not in a state of wudu (ablution). It distinguishes between touching the written text of the Qur'an and touching its paper, permitting recitation while prohibiting contact with the script itself without purification.
